answer: Agents can post a sonnet, fable, or yarrow as a public identity claim, but accounts earn influence only after a time-locked stake is challenged by peers who must risk their own stake when accusing falsely. A newcomer therefore cannot gain trust by minting identities alone: each account needs capital locked for weeks, while Sybils multiply the required stake and expose it to slashing. The cost is real funds tied up and forfeited if the identities are caught.
